hero.h1: From first draft to final call sheet
hero.sub: For indie directors, writers and line producers. Write the script, break it down and plan the shoot in one place. Every keystroke is written to your own browser first, and sync is yours to switch off. A year of the studio from about {{fms:price.from.day}} a day, nothing renews by itself, and it keeps working when the signal drops.
hero.note: Every tool is open on a sample feature, {{fms:dragon.scenes}} scenes long, so you can look around before you write.

stages.body: A screenplay writer for Tamil, Tanglish and English. The format sets itself as you type, drafts are numbered, and every scene heading becomes a scene the rest of the studio can use.
stages.bodyElsewhere: A screenplay writer in the standard format. It sets itself as you type, drafts are numbered, and every scene heading becomes a scene the rest of the studio can use.

stages.body: Place your beats on one of eleven story structures, check where the pacing sags, then give each planned shot a frame on the storyboard.
Auto-tag suggests what each scene needs and you accept what is right. Then build the shot list, lay scenes onto a stripboard, and print the sides for the day.

Move a scene to another day on the stripboard, and the day-out-of-days follows. Build that day’s call sheet from the board and print it or send it on WhatsApp. The budget is in rupees and starts from dated Chennai rates.
stages.bodyElsewhere: Move a scene to another day on the stripboard, and the day-out-of-days follows. Build that day’s call sheet from the board and print it or send it on WhatsApp. The budget is line by line and follows the money once the shoot begins.

stages.body: Everything you write is saved in your own browser first, and the studio installs like an app. Once you sign in, your films also sync so they reach your other devices; switch sync off in Settings and the browser copy stays either way. It works on set without a signal for up to 14 days after you last signed in on that device, then needs a connection once to check your sign-in. A backup to your own Google Drive is there if you want a second copy.

answers.h2: Four questions to ask before you sign in

items.q: Why sign in with Google if my work is local?
items.a: Sign-in is the door: it tells the studio who you are, so it can check your plan or free trial before it opens. Once you are in, your projects also sync to the studio's cloud to reach your other devices. You can switch sync off in Settings, and the copy in your browser stays either way.

items.q: Why does offline stop after 14 days?
items.a: It works on set without a signal for up to 14 days after you last signed in on that device. After that it needs a connection once, to check your sign-in and your plan again. Nothing you wrote is deleted while it waits.

items.q: How long is the free trial?
items.aHtml: Right now it is a free trial. The length is a studio setting, read live, so it is never typed here. It opens every module, needs no card, and does not hold a price: a plan costs what it costs on the day you buy it.

items.q: What leaves my browser, and when?
items.a: Your projects, when you are signed in and sync is on. A backup, when you connect your own Google Drive. The text you give an AI tool, when you run one with your own key, to the provider you chose. The studio also talks to its server to sign you in, check your plan or trial and take a payment through Razorpay. While it is open and you are signed in, the device checks in about every 30 seconds so your account stays on one device at a time, and the server sees that device's IP address and browser type. Signed in, it also sends daily counts of which tools are opened and the reason code when a save is refused, never anything you wrote; you can switch both off in Settings, under Privacy. Visit counts on the public pages are daily totals with no name on them. The privacy policy lists every record in full.
